files.Title: EchoHub.Client.AppOrchestrator
files.Summary: Central orchestrator for the EchoHub TUI client. Wires UI events to service calls and connection events to UI updates.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.AsyncRunner
files.Summary: Eliminates repeated Task.Run/try/catch/app.Invoke(ShowError) boilerplate. Runs async work on a background thread and routes exceptions to the UI.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.ChannelPasswordRequiredException
files.Summary: Thrown when joining a channel fails because a password is required or incorrect. The UI catches this to prompt the user and retry.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.ClientEncryptionService
files.Summary: Client-side encryption service. Uses the same AES-256-GCM format as the server so messages are encrypted end-to-end between client and server.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.ClipboardFiles
files.Summary: Reads file paths that live on the OS clipboard as a file list (e.g. after copying a file in Explorer/Finder/Nautilus), which terminals do not paste as text. Lets Ctrl+V attach a copied file directly instead of requiring the user to paste a raw path.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.ClipboardImage
files.Summary: Reads raw image data from the OS clipboard (e.g. an image copied from a browser, or a Win+Shift+S screenshot), which terminals cannot paste as text. Always returns PNG bytes: clipboard PNG data is passed through, clipboard bitmaps (CF_DIB) are re-encoded.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.JoinOutcome
files.Summary: Result of joining a channel: decrypted history plus, for end-to-end encrypted channels, the key envelope needed to unlock the room content key.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.NativeFolderPicker
files.Summary: Opens the OS-native folder chooser (Windows Explorer, macOS Finder, Linux GTK/KDE) by shelling out, so the TUI doesn't need a GUI toolkit reference. Returns when no native dialog can run, so callers can fall back to a configured path.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.OutgoingAttachment
files.Summary: One file to upload as part of a message. For end-to-end encrypted channels the stream is already ciphertext, is set (image/audio/file), and holds the room-encrypted ASCII art for images. For normal channels only and are set.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.PathSetup
files.Summary: Ensures the application's directory is on the system PATH so users can run 'echohub' from any terminal session.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.RoomKeyProtector
files.Summary: Encrypts cached room content keys at rest so the client config never holds them as plain base64. Windows uses DPAPI (current-user scope, format prefix "dp1:"). On other platforms the keys are AES-GCM encrypted with a per-user master key file stored next to the config with 0600 permissions (prefix "k1:") — without an OS keychain that is file-permission-level protection, not zero-knowledge: anyone who can read both the config and the key file can recover the room keys. Values with no recognized prefix are legacy plain-base64 keys from older clients; they load once and are re-encrypted. The room passphrase itself is never stored in any form.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.RoomKeyStore
files.Summary: Holds room content keys for end-to-end encrypted channels: in-memory for the active session, persisted per-server in the client config (like saved sessions) so users don't retype the passphrase every launch. Keys never leave this machine and are encrypted at rest by . Also tracks which channels are known to be end-to-end encrypted, so senders can refuse to emit plaintext into a room whose key isn't cached yet.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.RoomLockedException
files.Summary: Thrown when sending into an end-to-end encrypted channel whose room key isn't cached: without the key the message would leave the client as plaintext, which must never happen.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.Services.UpdateBackupService
files.Summary: Manages pre-update backups and rollback restoration for the auto-updater. Backup location: ~/.echohub/update-backup/

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Chat.AttachmentAction
files.Summary: An action a click on an attachment line can trigger.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Chat.AttachmentActionSpan
files.Summary: Inclusive column range on a chat line that triggers an attachment action when clicked.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Chat.ChatColors
files.Summary: Shared color attributes for chat rendering (timestamps, system messages).

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Chat.ChatLine
files.Summary: A single line in the chat, composed of colored segments.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Chat.ChatListSource
files.Summary: Custom list data source for chat messages with per-segment coloring.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Chat.ChatMessageManager
files.Summary: Owns chat message storage, formatting, and mutation. Fires when a channel's message list is modified so the UI layer can refresh.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Chat.ChatSegment
files.Summary: A colored text segment within a chat line.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.ChannelPasswordDialog
files.Summary: Prompts for a channel password when joining a protected channel. Returns the entered password, or null if the user cancels.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.ConnectDialog
files.Summary: A Terminal.Gui dialog for entering server connection and authentication details. Includes a saved servers selector when saved servers are available.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.ConnectDialogResult
files.Summary: Result returned from the connect dialog.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.ProfileAction
files.Summary: Action selected by the user in their own profile dialog.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.ProfileEditDialog
files.Summary: A Terminal.Gui dialog for editing the user's profile (display name, bio, nickname color).

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.ProfileEditResult
files.Summary: Result returned from the profile edit dialog.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.ProfileViewDialog
files.Summary: Dialog for viewing a user's server profile. Shows Edit Profile / Set Status buttons when viewing own profile.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.SearchDialog
files.Summary: Command-palette style search dialog (Ctrl+K) for navigating channels and triggering app actions.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.StatusDialog
files.Summary: A Terminal.Gui dialog for setting the user's status and status message.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Dialogs.StatusDialogResult
files.Summary: Result returned from the status dialog.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Helpers.DroppedFileParser
files.Summary: Recognizes a dragged-and-dropped file (or files) that a terminal delivers into the input as an absolute path. Terminals differ: some paste the whole path at once, others send it character by character; either way this checks whether the current input text resolves to existing file(s).

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Helpers.EmojiHelper
files.Summary: Converts emoji grapheme clusters to text shortcodes for safe TUI rendering. Terminal width calculations for emoji are unreliable across different terminals, so we replace them with fixed-width ASCII shortcodes for display only.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Helpers.HexColorHelper
files.Summary: Helper to parse hex colors to Terminal.Gui Attributes.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.Helpers.NickColorHelper
files.Summary: Deterministic per-nick colors for users who haven't picked a nickname color. The same nick always maps to the same palette entry (classic IRC client behavior), so a busy channel stays scannable without any configuration.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.ListSources.ChannelListSource
files.Summary: Custom list data source for colored channel list rendering. Active channel gets a > indicator, unread channels are bright with a count badge.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.ListSources.SearchListSource
files.Summary: List data source for the search dialog with filtering and colored rendering.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.ListSources.UserListSource
files.Summary: Custom list data source for the online users panel with per-user nickname colors.

files.Title: EchoHub.Client.UI.MainWindow
files.Summary: Main Terminal.Gui window for the EchoHub chat client.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.Constants.MessageConventions
files.Summary: Cross-protocol message conventions. Action messages (/me) use the IRC CTCP ACTION wire format 0x01 + "ACTION " + text + 0x01 as the stored content, so IRC clients interoperate natively (irssi's /me arrives in exactly this shape) and the TUI renders "* nick text". In end-to-end encrypted rooms the marker encrypts along with the text.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.Contracts.IEchoHubClient
files.Summary: Methods the server can invoke on connected clients.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.DTOs.AttachmentDto
files.Summary: A file attached to a message. holds the color-tag art for images (null otherwise). For end-to-end encrypted channels the content behind and the preview are ciphertext the server cannot read.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.DTOs.ChannelCryptoDto
files.Summary: Public crypto metadata for a channel — enough for a client to derive its join credential from a passphrase. Never includes the wrapped room key.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.DTOs.ChannelMetaDto
files.Summary: Human-facing summary of a channel (the /meta command). For encrypted channels the server still knows these figures — count, timestamps, and stored blob sizes — even though it cannot read the content itself. is the sum of stored attachment blob sizes plus message text length, so it is an estimate, not an exact on-disk total.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.DTOs.DeleteAccountRequest
files.Summary: Password re-confirmation for destructive self-service account actions.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.DTOs.RekeyChannelRequest
files.Summary: Passphrase change for an encrypted channel: the client proves knowledge of the old passphrase (old auth key), then supplies the re-wrapped room key under the new one.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.DTOs.ReplyRefDto
files.Summary: Reference to the message a reply targets. is treated exactly like message content on the wire: transport-encrypted, and for end-to-end encrypted rooms it is room ciphertext the client must decrypt (the server truncates only plaintext snippets). Null on a when the original message no longer exists.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.DTOs.UserDataExportDto
files.Summary: Everything the server holds about a user, as stored. For end-to-end encrypted rooms the message content in here is room ciphertext — the server cannot include plaintext it never had.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.Models.Attachment
files.Summary: A file attached to a message (image, audio, or any file). A message may carry zero or more attachments alongside its text content (Discord-style).

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.Models.AttachmentKind
files.Summary: The kind of a message attachment. Determines how the client renders it (ASCII preview for images, a play affordance for audio, a download line for files).

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.Models.InviteCode
files.Summary: A registration invite code. When the server runs with Server:Registration = "invite", new accounts (REST and IRC alike) require a valid, unexpired, not-fully-used code.

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.Security.RoomCrypto
files.Summary:
Client-side envelope encryption for private (end-to-end encrypted) channels.

Design: at creation the client generates a random 256-bit room content key (RCK) that encrypts all room content. The RCK is stored on the server wrapped (AES-GCM encrypted) by a key derived from the passphrase, next to a BCrypt hash of a separately derived auth key used as the join gate. The passphrase, the key-encryption key, and the RCK never leave the client, so the server can gate joins and count/measure content without being able to read it. Changing the passphrase only re-wraps the RCK — history is never re-encrypted.

Derivation: PBKDF2-SHA256(passphrase, salt, 210000 iterations) → 64 bytes; first 32 bytes are the auth key (sent to the server as lowercase hex), last 32 bytes are the key-encryption key (never sent).

files.Title: EchoHub.Core.Services.AsciiBannerService
files.Summary: Renders short text as a 5-row block-character banner (the /banner command). Entirely local — a hand-rolled figlet-style font, no dependencies, no network. Output is plain message content, so it travels (and encrypts) like any other text.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Irc.IrcClientConnection
files.Summary: Manages a single IRC client TCP connection.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Irc.IrcMessage
files.Summary: Parsed representation of an IRC protocol line. Format: [:prefix] COMMAND [params...] [:trailing]

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Config.ServerLogsOptions
files.Summary: Live server-log room settings, bound from the "ServerLogs" config section (env override: ServerLogs__Enabled etc.). When enabled, a read-only system channel is auto-created and log events are streamed to it live — log lines are never stored as messages in the database; the rolling Serilog log files remain the only persistence.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Config.SpamOptions
files.Summary: Anti-spam thresholds, bound from the "Spam" config section. Defaults are lenient enough that a fast typist never trips them; Mods and above are always exempt.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Config.UploadLimits
files.Summary: Admin-configurable upload limits, bound from the Uploads configuration section. Sizes are expressed in megabytes in configuration; the *Bytes accessors convert them for enforcement. Every default mirrors so an absent or partial Uploads section preserves the historical built-in limits.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Controllers.InvitesController
files.Summary: Invite-code management for invite-gated registration (Admin+ only). Codes live in this server's own database — there is no central service.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Services.DirectoryClaimStore
files.Summary:
Persists and exposes the EchoHubSpace directory claim — the opaque token issued on first registration and the row's stable ServerId. Also surfaces ephemeral registration status (success/failure code, conflicting hosts) for operator-facing endpoints.

Persistence uses atomic write (tmp + rename). Treat the file contents as a secret.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Services.MuteExpirationService
files.Summary: Background service that periodically unmutes users whose timed mute has expired.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Services.ServerLogs.LogBacklogEntry
files.Summary: A backlog entry read from the log file: one timestamped log line plus any continuation lines (exception stack traces) that followed it.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Services.ServerLogs.ServerLogsService
files.Summary: Shared logic for the live log room: room identity, the role gate, and reading the backlog tail from the current rolling log file. The file stays the only persistence — log lines are never stored as messages.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Services.ServerLogs.ServerLogsSink
files.Summary: Serilog sink feeding the live log room. Events are queued in a bounded drop-oldest buffer and consumed by ; nothing is written to the database. Events emitted by the streaming pipeline itself (the stream service and SignalR transport internals) are dropped here so a broadcast that logs — e.g. a transport warning on a dead connection — can never enter a log → broadcast → log feedback loop.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Services.ServerLogs.ServerLogsStreamService
files.Summary:
Streams queued log events to the live log room as ephemeral messages: SignalR only (the IRC gateway never sees them) and no database rows. Ensures the room exists before streaming, recreating it on the fly if it was deleted.

This class must never log from its streaming path — its namespace is excluded by as a second line of defense, but the primary rule is simply not to log per event, otherwise every streamed line would spawn another.

files.Title: EchoHub.Server.Services.SpamGuard
files.Summary: In-memory, per-user spam protection consulted from (messages, joins) and (channel creation), so every ingress protocol — SignalR and IRC alike — shares the same limits. State is per-process and never persisted; auto-mutes land in the normal mute store. Operates only on content the server already stores (for end-to-end encrypted rooms that is ciphertext) — nothing is decrypted.
